Patient Name: Satnam Singh
Age/Sex: 27 / Male
IP No: IP-990812

Treating Consultant: Dr. Rajesh Mehta, MS (General Surgery)
Diagnosis: Acute Appendicitis

Clinical History:
Patient presented with acute right lower quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and low-grade fever for 1 day. Clinical examination revealed tenderness in right iliac fossa (McBurney's point tenderness).

Investigations:
Ultrasound of abdomen confirmed acutely inflamed appendix measuring 9mm with periappendiceal fluid. WBC count was 14,500/mm3.

Procedure Performed:
Laparoscopic Appendectomy performed on 14-08-2026 under General Anesthesia by Dr. Rajesh Mehta. Appendix was found to be retrocecal, congested, and gangrenous. Successful removal of appendix done. Hemostasis achieved. Specimen sent for histopathology.

Post-operative Course:
Uneventful. Patient was started on liquid diet on post-op day 1, progressed to normal diet on day 2. Mobilized active. Afebrile. Vitals stable. Wound healing well.

Discharge Advice:
- Rest for 1 week.
- Tab Cefuroxime 500mg twice daily for 5 days.
- Tab Paracetamol 650mg as needed for pain.
- Follow up in OPD after 7 days for suture check.

Dr. Rajesh Mehta, MS
SMC Reg No: MMC-2015-08-3294

Patient Name: Priyashe Gupta

Date of Discharge: 12-08-2026

Treating Consultant: Dr. Vikram Joshi, MS (General Surgery)
Diagnosis: Cholelithiasis (Gallstones with Chronic Cholecystitis)

Clinical History:
Patient presented with recurrent episodes of colicky right upper quadrant pain radiating to the back, associated with fatty meals. Ultrasound showed multiple small gallstones with gallbladder wall thickening (4mm).

Procedure Performed:
Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy performed on 10-08-2026 under General Anesthesia by Dr. Vikram Joshi. Intra-operatively, gallbladder was found to be chronically inflamed and adhered to omentum. Adhesiolysis done. Cystic duct and artery dissected, clipped, and divided. Gallbladder dissected off the liver bed and extracted. Hemostasis confirmed.

Post-operative Course:
Stable. Tolerating oral feeds. Mobilized. Pain controlled with oral analgesics. Discharge authorized on 12-08-2026.

Discharge Advice:
- Avoid fatty meals for 3 weeks.
- Tab Pantoprazole 40mg once daily before breakfast for 10 days.
- Tab Tramadol 50mg as needed for pain.

Dr. Vikram Joshi, MS
SMC Reg No: GMC-2012-04-1102

Diagnosis: Acute Gastroenteritis with Moderate Dehydration

Clinical History:
Patient presented with severe watery diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal cramps for 2 days. He had dry mucous membranes, tachycardia (110 bpm), and mild hypotension (100/60 mmHg).

Investigations:
Stool culture showed no growth. Blood work showed mild hypokalemia (K+: 3.2 mEq/L) and elevated hematocrit indicating hemoconcentration.

Treatment Protocol:
Admitted for intravenous rehydration and correction of electrolytes. Administered IV fluids (Normal Saline and Ringer Lactate with Potassium supplementation). IV antibiotics (Metronidazole and Ceftriaxone) administered.

Condition at Discharge:
Clinically stable. Hydration restored. Potassium normalized. Tolerating soft diet. Vitals normal.
